question_stem:
A small charged glass bead of weight 5.4 × 10^{-5} N is initially at rest at point A in a vacuum. The
bead then falls through a uniform horizontal electric field as it moves in a straight line to point B, as
illustrated in Fig. 2.1.
The electric field strength is 1.3 × 10^{4} V m^{-1}. The charge on the bead is –3.7 × 10^{-9} C.
question_stem_latex:
A small charged glass bead of weight $5.4 \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{N}$ is initially at rest at point A in a vacuum. The
bead then falls through a uniform horizontal electric field as it moves in a straight line to point B, as
illustrated in Fig. 2.1.
The electric field strength is $1.3 \times 10^{4}\,\mathrm{V}\,\mathrm{m}^{-1}$. The charge on the bead is –$3.7 \times 10^{-9}\,\mathrm{C}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question_text:
Describe how two metal plates could be used to produce the electric field. Numerical values
are not required.
parts.question_text_latex:
Describe how two metal plates could be used to produce the electric field. Numerical values
are not required.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
Determine the magnitude of the electric force acting on the bead.
electric force = N
parts.question_text_latex:
Determine the magnitude of the electric force acting on the bead.
$electric force = N $

parts.label: (c)
parts.question_text:
Use your answer in (b) and the weight of the bead to show that the resultant force acting on it
is 7.2 × 10^{-5} N.
parts.question_text_latex:
Use your answer in (b) and the weight of the bead to show that the resultant force acting on it
is $7.2 \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{N}$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.question_text:
Explain why the resultant force on the bead of 7.2 × 10^{-5} N is constant as the bead moves
along path AB.
parts.question_text_latex:
Explain why the resultant force on the bead of $7.2 \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{N}$ is constant as the bead moves
along path AB.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.question_text:
Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of the bead along the path AB.
acceleration = m s ^{2}
parts.question_text_latex:
Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of the bead along the path AB.
$acceleration = m s ^{2} $

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.question_text_latex:
The path AB has length 0.58 m.
Use your answer in (i) to determine the speed of the bead at point B.
$speed = m s ^{1} $
